plan: [This is a second-price auction (highest pays the second-highest). Truthful bidding is a dominant strategy regardless of others' strategies and independent draws. With no prior rounds to learn from and my value = $31, I should bid my true value to maximize expected long-run profit and avoid regret from misreporting.]

[In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true private value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected surplus and avoids overpaying. With value = $6, you win exactly when the second-highest bid is below $6 and then pay that second-highest amount. Independent redraws and only one round don't change this. Therefore bid your true value, rounded to the allowed increment.]

[This is a second-price auction where bidding your true private value is a dominant strategy. My value is $0, so I should bid $0. Any positive bid risks winning and paying a positive second-highest bid, yielding negative profit. Bidding $0 never yields negative payoff (ties that win pay $0), so it maximizes long-run expected profit given independent draws.]
